function: CSI (eigenvector) feedback: BiLSTM autoencoder compresses the downlink eigenvector at the UE and reconstructs it at the gNB, with variable input length and feedback bits (p. 3, p. 4).
system: Massive MIMO-OFDM, NT = 32 gNB antennas, NR = 4 UE antennas, 3, 6 or 12 subbands; carrier frequency not stated; no RIS (p. 2, p. 8).
method: BiLSTM autoencoder (ABLNet) with feedback bit control unit, end-to-end SGCS reconstruction loss, 500 epochs; UE-first separate training of encoders and general decoder (p. 4, p. 5, p. 7, p. 8).
data_channel: 3GPP CDL-A and CDL-C channels (30 ns delay spread) simulated by the authors; 50,000 training and 1,000 test eigenvectors per subband number (p. 7, p. 8).
test_conditions: Trained and tested on the same channel (CDL-A or CDL-C) and subband numbers 3, 6, 12; no unseen channel, antenna number or band tested (p. 8, p. 9).
baselines: eTypeII codebook (non-learned); EVCsiNet and Transformer (learned CSI feedback, with adaptive-input and multi-decoder variants); BiLSTMNet (own fixed-length variant) (p. 8, p. 9, p. 10).
metrics: SGCS of eigenvector recovery, link-level BLER versus SNR, CDF of SGCS, average feedback bits, trainable parameters and FLOPs (p. 8, p. 9, p. 10).
complexity: Trainable parameters and FLOPs (Table II): ABLNet 14.75e6 and 32.40e7; EVCsiNet 6.98e6 and 1.41e7; Transformer 23.95e6 and 51.29e7 (p. 8).
q1_support: p. 7: "The clustered delay line (CDL) channel model defined in the 3GPP is adapted to generate data samples" - CDL-A and CDL-C profiles with 30 ns delay spread (p. 8).
q2_support: p. 8: "the sizes of training and testing datasets are 50,000 and 1,000 respectively" - models are trained and tested on the same CDL channel and the same subband numbers (3, 6, 12); no unseen channel, antenna number or band is tested.
q3_support: p. 10: "EVCsiNet and Transformer at Q = 120 bits. Moreover, for the traditional CSI feedback scheme, i.e., eTypeII" - eTypeII is the non-learned baseline, EVCsiNet and Transformer are earlier learned CSI feedback models; BiLSTMNet is a variant of ABLNet and is not counted.
q4_support: p. 8: "the model complexity of different feedback schemes are analyzed in terms of trainable parameters and floating point operations (FLOPs)" - Table II gives both for ABLNet, EVCsiNet and Transformer.
q5_support: p. 7: "the 3GPP is adapted to generate data samples" - self-generated 3GPP CDL data; no link, repository or DOI for code or data anywhere in the paper.
notes: Preprint (arXiv v1). Area 2: eigenvector-based CSI feedback. q1: the paper says only that the CDL model is defined in the 3GPP and does not name TR 38.901, but CDL-A and CDL-C are TR 38.901 profiles; the reviewer may confirm. q2: the model is trained with subband numbers 3, 6 and 12 together and tested on the same ones (p. 5, p. 8); the paper does not say that any tested bit number lies outside the trained set, and the different CSI distributions of Fig. 14 (p. 11) are separate encoders per UE on whose data the general decoder is trained, so no unseen condition is stated. q3: BiLSTMNet and the gNB-first strategy (p. 11) are variants of the proposed scheme and are not counted as learned baselines.
